[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.aws_eks_cluster.cluster` should wait for `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.cluster` so the EKS control-plane role permissions are attached before cluster creation and remain available through cluster deletion; the AWS provider documentation recommends this explicit ordering.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The EKS cluster role is referenced, but the cluster can be created before its managed IAM policies are reconciled. The AWS provider documentation specifically recommends ordering cluster creation after the role permissions; without this edge, cluster deletion can also occur before those permissions are removed.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The EKS cluster references the IAM role, but not the role's policy attachments. The AWS provider documentation recommends an explicit dependency on the cluster role permissions so EKS has them before cluster handling and can clean up managed infrastructure during deletion.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
aws_eks_cluster.cluster only references aws_iam_role.cluster.arn, but the required cluster policies are attached by aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.cluster, which has no ordering edge to the cluster. The AWS provider documents that the EKS cluster must depend on the IAM role policy attachments, otherwise EKS cannot create/delete managed EC2 infrastructure (e.g. security groups) because the role lacks AmazonEKSClusterPolicy at the time. Add `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.cluster]` to the cluster.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
aws_eks_cluster.cluster references aws_iam_role.cluster.arn but has no ordering dependency on aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.cluster. The EKS control plane requires its IAM role to already carry AmazonEKSClusterPolicy (and the other EKS policies) when it is created; otherwise cluster creation can fail and EKS cannot manage/clean up its EC2 infrastructure (e.g. security groups) on deletion. The provider documentation explicitly recommends depends_on for the role-policy attachment.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
aws_eks_cluster.cluster references aws_iam_role.cluster.arn but not aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.cluster, which attaches the required AmazonEKSClusterPolicy and other policies. Because aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive is a separate resource, Terraform has no ordering edge, and EKS validates the cluster role's permissions during create and needs them during delete of EKS-managed infrastructure. The provider documentation explicitly requires depends_on on the role policy attachments here.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.aws_eks_cluster.cluster only depends on :resource.aws_iam_role.cluster (via role_arn), but EKS validates at CreateCluster time that the cluster role carries the required managed policies (AmazonEKSClusterPolicy etc.). If :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.cluster hasn't applied yet, cluster creation fails. It should depend on the policy attachment resource.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_eks_cluster.cluster uses aws_iam_role.cluster.arn but has no dependency on aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.cluster. EKS validates the cluster role's permissions at cluster creation, so the cluster must be created only after the AmazonEKSClusterPolicy (and related policies) are attached, otherwise cluster creation fails with an authorization error.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
`:module.eks_node_group_al2023` should wait for `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.eks_node_group` so the managed node group's role permissions are in place before node-group lifecycle operations.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The managed node group module receives the node role ARN, but has no dependency on the role's managed-policy reconciliation. EKS node group provisioning should wait until the worker-node policies are attached; the AWS provider documentation recommends this ordering for node groups.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The managed node group module receives the node role ARN but does not depend on the role's managed policy attachments. The AWS provider documentation recommends ensuring node-role permissions exist before EKS Node Group handling, including for cleanup of EC2 instances and network interfaces.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
module.eks_node_group_al2023 references aws_iam_role.eks_node_group.arn (create_iam_role = false), but that role's worker-node policies are attached by aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.eks_node_group, which has no ordering edge to the node group. The managed node group's instances will fail to join the cluster (missing AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy etc.) if the node group is created before the attachments. Add `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.eks_node_group]` to the node group module.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
module.eks_node_group_al2023 sets node_role_arn = aws_iam_role.eks_node_group.arn but has no ordering dependency on aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.eks_node_group. The EKS managed node group validates that the node IAM role already has the required policies (AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy, ECR read-only, etc.); without the attachment in place, node group creation can fail or nodes fail to join the cluster.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
module.eks_node_group_al2023 (which creates the aws_eks_node_group) references aws_iam_role.eks_node_group.arn but not aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.eks_node_group, which attaches the required AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy/AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy/AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly policies. Without an edge to the attachment, the node group may be created before the role's policies are attached, and EKS validates the node role permissions on node group create and needs them on delete. The provider docs require depends_on on the role policy attachments for aws_eks_node_group.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:module.eks_node_group_al2023 references :resource.aws_iam_role.eks_node_group via node_role_arn, but not the managed policy attachments. Node group instances launched before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.eks_node_group applies lack AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy/AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy and will never join the cluster.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
:module.eks_node_group_al2023 only depends on :resource.aws_iam_role.eks_node_group via its node_role_arn, but not on :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.eks_node_group, which attaches the required worker policies (AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy, AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly, etc.). If the managed node group is provisioned before the policy attachments propagate, worker nodes cannot join the cluster. :module.eks_node_group_al2023 should wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.eks_node_group (e.g. an explicit depends_on, since only the bare role ARN is referenced).

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
module.eks_node_group_al2023 depends on aws_iam_role.eks_node_group.arn but not on aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.eks_node_group. Managed node group creation requires the node instance role to already have AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy and AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly attached; the attachment resource may otherwise be applied in parallel with (or after) the node group.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.aws_eks_addon.aws_ebs_csi_driver` should wait for `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.ebs_csi_controller_sa` so the CSI driver's service-account role has its required permissions before the add-on starts running.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The EBS CSI add-on is configured with the controller service-account role, but its managed policy attachments are reconciled independently. Ensure the permissions exist before the add-on is installed so its controller does not start without the required AWS access.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The EBS CSI EKS add-on is configured to use this service-account role, but it depends only on the role itself, not its managed policy attachments. The provider documentation says the role must have the add-on's required permissions; create the attachments before installing the add-on to avoid starting it without those permissions.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.aws_eks_addon.aws_ebs_csi_driver passes service_account_role_arn = :resource.aws_iam_role.ebs_csi_controller_sa but does not depend on :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.ebs_csi_controller_sa. If the AmazonEBSCSIDriverPolicy is not yet attached when the addon is installed, the CSI controller pods will fail to provision volumes (and on first install may error out).

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_eks_addon.aws_ebs_csi_driver sets service_account_role_arn from aws_iam_role.ebs_csi_controller_sa.arn but does not depend on aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.ebs_csi_controller_sa. The addon provider docs require the service-account role to already have the IAM permissions the addon needs; if the addon is applied before the AmazonEBSCSIDriverPolicy attachment, the driver pods fail authorization.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.aws_eks_addon.adot` should wait for `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.adot_collector` so the collector's service-account role permissions are attached before the add-on starts running.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
This add-on references the ADOT IAM role, but its required managed policies are reconciled separately. Make the add-on wait for the role's policy attachments so the add-on does not start before its service account has the permissions it needs.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The ADOT add-on uses this IAM role, but the add-on has no dependency on the role's managed policy attachments. Since the configured role must have the permissions required by the add-on, ensure those permissions are attached before installing it.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.aws_eks_addon.adot references :resource.aws_iam_role.adot_collector via service_account_role_arn but not its policy attachments; if :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.adot_collector applies after the addon, the ADOT collector cannot write to Prometheus/X-Ray/CloudWatch.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_eks_addon.adot sets service_account_role_arn from aws_iam_role.adot_collector.arn but does not depend on aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.adot_collector. The addon provider docs require the service-account role to already have the IAM permissions the addon needs; if the addon is applied before the Prometheus/X-Ray/CloudWatch policy attachments, the collector pods fail authorization.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.aws_eks_cluster.cluster` should wait for `:resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster` so EKS logging uses the explicitly configured log group (including its retention and KMS settings) rather than creating or using it before those settings are applied.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
When EKS control-plane logging is enabled, EKS can create the cluster log group automatically. Create the Terraform-managed group first so EKS uses the configured group (including retention and KMS settings), rather than racing its creation or creating it with defaults.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The cluster log group is configured for the EKS cluster's control-plane logs, but the cluster can be created concurrently with that log group. Ordering the cluster after the log group avoids a creation race and ensures the configured group exists before EKS starts sending logs.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
When :var.eks_enabled_log_types is non-empty, EKS auto-creates /aws/eks/<name>/cluster. If :resource.aws_eks_cluster.cluster is created before :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster, EKS may create the group first and Terraform's create then fails with "already exists". :resource.aws_eks_cluster.cluster should be ordered after the log group.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
:resource.aws_eks_cluster.cluster has no dependency on :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster, but when var.eks_enabled_log_types is non-empty the EKS control plane starts writing to /aws/eks/${var.name_prefix}/cluster as soon as the cluster is created. If the log group is created after the cluster, CloudWatch auto-creates it and Terraform fails with "ResourceAlreadyExistsException". :resource.aws_eks_cluster.cluster should wait for :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster to exist first (e.g. an explicit depends_on, since no attribute reference links them).

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_eks_cluster.cluster has no dependency on aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster. If the cluster is created before the log group, EKS/CloudWatch auto-creates /aws/eks/${var.name_prefix}/cluster on first log write, causing the Terraform aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster creation to collide and its retention_in_days setting to be lost.

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.aws_eks_addon.amazon_cloudwatch_observability has a depends_on for :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_performance only. The addon's Fluent Bit agent also auto-creates the application/host/dataplane log groups, so :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_application can race the addon (or already exist when Terraform tries to create it, breaking retention management). It needs the same ordering.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_eks_addon.amazon_cloudwatch_observability only depends_on aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_performance, but the addon's agent also writes to the application log group. Without aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_application being created first, the agent auto-creates it and Terraform's log group creation will conflict / lose its retention_in_days=180.

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
Same race as the performance/application groups: :resource.aws_eks_addon.amazon_cloudwatch_observability creates the dataplane Container Insights log group if absent, so it must not be created before :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_dataplane.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_eks_addon.amazon_cloudwatch_observability only depends_on aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_performance, but the addon's agent also writes to the dataplane log group. Without aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_dataplane being created first, the agent auto-creates it and Terraform's log group creation will conflict / lose its retention_in_days=180.

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
Same race as the performance/application groups: :resource.aws_eks_addon.amazon_cloudwatch_observability creates the host Container Insights log group if absent, so it must not be created before :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_host.

----------------------------------------
